environment.description: Same application deployed on EC2 c5.large running in a chroot jail under /opt/app-jail. The chroot environment was provisioned using debootstrap with a minimal filesystem containing only the Ruby runtime, application code, and required shared libraries. The PostgreSQL connection uses a restricted database role 'app_readonly_profile' that has column-level privileges: SELECT on all user columns, but UPDATE restricted to ONLY (name, avatar_url, billing_email) on the users table via PostgreSQL column-level GRANT. The database role has no UPDATE privilege on the 'role', 'is_admin', 'api_key', or 'internal_notes' columns. Additionally, the chroot contains no /etc/passwd, no credential files, and the process runs under a dedicated UID (65534) with no supplementary groups. The pg_hba.conf entry for this role enforces SSL client certificate authentication from the jail's loopback interface only.

config.database_grants: GRANT SELECT ON users TO app_readonly_profile; GRANT UPDATE (name, avatar_url, billing_email) ON users TO app_readonly_profile;
config.chroot_contents: ruby runtime, app code, libpq, libssl - no /etc/passwd, no credential files
